topic: Why a 25-minute timer beats a to-do list

ideas.title: The list that grew, the work that didn't
ideas.logline: Alex admits his to-do list grew every morning while nothing got started, then shows the one-question start screen.
ideas.rationale: Relatable pain from AUDIENCE.md plus a real build decision; existing example screens cover the product part.

ideas.title: Choosing is the work you avoid
ideas.logline: A long list forces a decision before any work starts; one task removes the decision.
ideas.rationale: Clear thought, but weaker story without the dev-diary frame.

ideas.title: I deleted my to-do list for a week
ideas.logline: Alex runs one task per timer for a week and reports honestly.
ideas.rationale: Strong story, but needs a week of real footage and risks sounding like an outcome promise.

ideas.title: Why my timer has no streaks
ideas.logline: Missing a day should not cost you anything; the app keeps no streaks.
ideas.rationale: Confirmed fact (no streaks), but a separate topic; better as its own video.

ideas.title: The email I opened instead of working
ideas.logline: A notification card plays the distraction; the timer answers it.
ideas.rationale: Visual and quick, less authentic as a standalone; works as a beat inside i01.

ideas.title: Pomodoro didn't work for me — until one task
ideas.logline: Alex says classic pomodoro failed because he never picked the task first.
ideas.rationale: Cheap to film, honest; low visual change.

ideas.title: Building the start screen in public
ideas.logline: Blockout → example UI of the one-question start screen.
ideas.rationale: Good for the pillar, but no viewer pain in the hook.

ideas.title: 3 of 5 beta features: what's next
ideas.logline: Beta progress update with the confirmed milestone.
ideas.rationale: Uses a confirmed fact, but an update without a thought is weak.

ideas.title: A to-do list vs a timer, side by side
ideas.logline: Split screen: growing list on one side, one running timer on the other.
ideas.rationale: Readable, but risks implying an outcome comparison we cannot back.

ideas.title: What breaks your focus? Viewers answer
ideas.logline: Collect real comments about distraction and react.
ideas.rationale: Needs real comments first; fictional ones would need labels.

top.why: Highest fit: a real pain from the audience doc, told by Alex at the desk, paid off by an existing example screen and confirmed facts.
Best story, kept as a follow-up once a real week of footage exists.
Confirmed fact (no streaks) and strong product fit; used as the payoff line here and kept as its own future video.
